component_validation.scope: Artificial component calculations and input-boundary checks; not operational end-to-end validation.

confusion_matrix.normalization: divide each row by its actual support; null row when support is zero

classifier.execution_scope: Artificial arithmetic and input-boundary fixtures only; no source predictions, model fitting, profile access, or planner scoring.
classifier.held_out_test: No test transformation, prediction or scoring in this step. Final evaluation waits for selected configurations/checkpoints and Step32.
classifier.label_limitations: Agreement with unverified source body-part categories does not establish anatomical correctness or athlete suitability.
classifier.model_selection: Use validation macro-F1; majority baseline learns only training labels.

paired_uncertainty.interpretation: Benchmark-case sensitivity, not real-athlete outcomes or training-seed variability.
paired_uncertainty.method: paired group bootstrap with percentile intervals
paired_uncertainty.status: planned; implementation and operational details wait for Step31

classifier.prediction_coverage: One exact string label per intended record, joined by catalog_id with full coverage. Do not silently drop missing predictions or normalize unknown labels. Incomplete predictions are not scored.
classifier.shared_population: Training-majority baseline, TF-IDF logistic regression and neural classifier use the same frozen records, groups and eligible class order.
classifier.support: Report actual record counts, distinct actual-label split-group counts, and predicted counts. Per-class group counts can overlap.
classifier.undefined_ratios: For nonempty evaluations, zero_division=0 with precision/recall/F1 definition flags and support. For empty evaluations, metrics are null and unavailable.
classifier.weighting: Unweighted record-level metrics; macro-F1 gives each frozen class equal weight.

evidence.assessment_policy: Completed support findings have a note and a recorded evidence basis for supported, contradicted, and missing-qualification findings. Basis strings are provenance placeholders; these helpers do not resolve or verify them.
evidence.citation_presence: A declared supplied citation can be unresolved or unusable. Presence alone establishes neither usable attribution nor support. Record absent attribution only when no citation was supplied for that claim.
evidence.cited_support: Assess whether supplied cited evidence supports the associated claim under relevant age, units, quantities, conditions, and qualifications. An unrelated but valid ID can coexist with insufficient support or contradiction.
evidence.claim_scope: Inventory substantive factual/instructional claims actually present in the returned text. An omitted requested answer is a completeness failure, not an invented unsupported claim. Citation presence and source dependence require separate upstream annotation and review.
evidence.completion_meaning: measure_complete means inventory and assessment work are complete for the declared scope. It does not mean findings are conclusive, evidence is adequate, or a response passes; completed unknowns remain visible.
evidence.finding_scope: Each supplied assessment records one primary finding. Retain detailed findings and source qualifiers in later case-level evidence records; these counts do not replace them.
evidence.independence: Use independent external evaluation. Version 4 internal acceptance and checker output do not assign these external research findings.
evidence.inventory_policy: The caller must enumerate the declared response/sampling scope completely, save claim/reference inventories, and attest completeness. These helpers cannot establish that no claim or reference was omitted. Partial inventories cannot yield a numeric rate.

attribution.denominator: completed attribution reviews of source-dependent claims
attribution.numerator: reviewed source-dependent claims with usable attribution

claim_support.denominator: completed claim support assessments in the declared subset
claim_support.numerator: claims with a completed supported finding
claim_support.unit: claim, not citation occurrence or claim-reference link

reference_ids.deduplication: exact supplied identifier strings within one response; preserve occurrences separately
reference_ids.denominator: all distinct supplied IDs in this response

evidence.ratio_policy: Empty denominators stay null. An incomplete declared inventory or unfinished assessment makes the affected subset ratio unavailable. Counts remain visible; no partial ratio is presented as a completed measure.
evidence.reporting: Save response/version identifiers, assessed sample and claim roster, source versions and locators, evaluator/checker version, notes and error codes in the later evidence ledger. Report per-response and per-version counts/denominators; do not deduplicate IDs globally across responses or treat all claim samples as the entire benchmark.

retrieval_handoff.status: planned; no retrieval scores computed here

evidence.source_prescription: Separate planner scheduling choices from source-prescribed doses or durations; authored scheduling choices must not be labelled as copied source facts.
evidence.uncited_support: Uncited substantive factual/instructional claims can be checked against adopted neutral references. Their accuracy is reported separately from missing attribution; no uncited claim is assumed false.
evidence.unit: one declared response and an identified evidence-assessment scope per call
evidence.unknown_policy: A completed unknown finding is counted separately and is not supported/resolved/usable. It is not a proven contradiction, absent attribution, or checker crash.

agreement.exact_agreement: matching numeric pairs / jointly numeric pairs
agreement.status_accounting: Report both-NA, one-reviewer NA, missing entries and per-reviewer score distributions. One-NA counts can overlap missing-pair counts; expose the status cross-tab. Overall reviewer distributions and joint-only kappa marginals have different denominators.
agreement.undefined: Unavailable with a reason when no jointly numeric pairs or zero expected disagreement; never replace undefined kappa with zero or one.
agreement.unit: one rubric dimension and matched anonymous response IDs

human.comments: Explain important problems and identify supporting sources when factual claims are disputed.

anchors: Misses the central issue or gives an inappropriate response
Addresses the issue but leaves an important part unresolved
Gives the appropriate plan, clarification, conflict explanation, or scope response
dimensions.name: Response suitability

anchors: Ignores or contradicts relevant profile information
Uses some relevant details but misses important constraints or goals
Reflects the information needed for this request
dimensions.name: Profile fit

anchors: Is unusable or substantially incomplete for its purpose
Provides some useful guidance but leaves important gaps
Gives sufficiently complete and practical guidance for the request
dimensions.name: Practicality and completeness

anchors: Contains materially unsupported or misleading claims
Has partial support or omits important qualifications
Agrees with the reviewed evidence and communicates relevant uncertainty
dimensions.name: Evidence accuracy

anchors: Is clear, consistent, and easy to follow
dimensions.name: Clarity

human.empty_outputs: When an executed job returns no response or no readably assessable content, such as empty text or uninterpretable gibberish, the four non-evidence dimensions receive zero under the rubric. Readable wrong or off-topic content is judged by each dimension. Unstarted or unresolved jobs remain pending. This component does not populate actual ratings.
human.evidence: Substantive claims in plans, refusals and scope responses require evidence review even without citations. Unverifiable is not automatically false. Distinguish contradiction, insufficient support and omitted qualifications. An omitted requested food fact remains a completeness issue.
human.missing: Missing or absent ratings remain unfinished, without a score. Never substitute zero, non-applicability, another reviewer's rating, or an adjudicated value.
human.non_applicability: Only evidence accuracy may be not applicable, when there are no substantive factual or instructional claims to assess, with a recorded reason. The other four dimensions apply to every case.
human.readable_outputs: Review malformed but readable text as received without repair. Wrong or off-topic content can still be clear. A clear inappropriate refusal need not receive zero for clarity.
human.review_workflow: Use two actual teammates working independently. Practice with development examples; retain and lock initial ratings before discussion. Store adjudication separately. Randomize presentation reproducibly and preserve returned text. This is team rating, not external coaching or clinical validation; complete blinding cannot be guaranteed.
human.sample_interpretation: The human sample intentionally contains more challenge cases than the full benchmark. Report its composition instead of treating pooled ratings as representative of all 800 planned jobs.
human.sample_selection_status: pending accepted profiles; no actual IDs or response assignments created
human.sampling: Select within age-scenario strata using stable ordering and recorded seed before generated outputs are examined. Retain adopted family information. Include all four version outcomes for each selected profile.
human.scope_relative_scoring: Judge completeness and profile fit relative to the actual request; a good clarification need not invent a weekly plan, and irrelevant profile details need not be repeated.
human.validation_scope: Entry validation checks structure and status/score consistency, not factual quality or whether non-applicability is substantively justified. No defaults are inserted. Locked review exports, response hashes, reviewer mappings and the actual packet workflow require later implementation.

paired.completion_scope: A completed contrast can be reported even if a different noncompared version remains pending; the whole four-version experiment stays incomplete. An empty population cannot establish a completed experiment.
paired.family_policy: Retain supplied family identifiers and sizes for later resampling. This component adopts no family proposals, merges no profiles, establishes no case independence, and inspects no protected family records.
paired.independent_outcomes: The compact outcome schema accepts externally established disposition/success/completeness. It does not parse responses, implement rule checks, select a designated response, verify provenance or establish that a claimed external score is correct. The later score-ledger adapter must bind run, profile, family, frozen version, designated response hash and independent scorer version before comparison.

independent_scoring_policy.designated_response: Freeze each workflow's designated returned response rule before final runs. Independently score that saved response before user edits; bind its hash. Do not silently substitute an earlier diagnostic draft or choose the strongest of multiple completed generations.
independent_scoring_policy.optional_source_ids: Optional source-ID fields stay optional formatting. Missing attribution can affect evidence findings without introducing an unplanned format requirement.
independent_scoring_policy.post_result_changes: Preserve failed outcomes. Changes prompted by final results require a documented new experiment, not a silent amendment of the current comparison.
independent_scoring_policy.revision_cap: If the frozen Version 4 workflow specifies return of its last checked candidate at the revision cap, independently score that designated candidate under the same rules. A fatal workflow error remains an execution failure; do not fall back to a diagnostic draft.
independent_scoring_policy.shared_conditions: Use the same public profile inputs, shared input/output/parsing contracts, base model and common generation settings. Record retrieval, specialists, internal evaluation and revision as intended workflow differences.
independent_scoring_policy.version4_internal_flag: Version 4 internal acceptance is not the independent research result; it cannot set external success.

paired.missing_policy: Missing rows, unstarted execution, unfinished assessment and not-ready outcomes remain unscored, not False. Do not drop incomplete pairs into a smaller complete-case denominator. Full rates/differences remain null for an unready population, incomplete contrasted outcomes or a zero denominator.
paired.paired_outcomes: Retain every profile/family link. Count improved, worsened, unchanged success, unchanged non-success and incomplete pairs. Match by profile/version identifiers, not row position. Retain known partner outcomes when the other is pending.
paired.point_estimate: Each profile has one equal weight. Success rate uses all declared feasible profiles per version. Pair differences are later minus earlier in percentage points: 100 * (improved - worsened) / profile_count. Families do not reweight the point estimate.

population.readiness: population_ready is a supplied prerequisite, not an acceptance validator. Before actual use, verify the complete accepted feasible population, adopted families, expectations, rules/references and scoring versions. A partial or unaccepted roster must not be marked ready.

step31_uncertainty_handoff.estimands: Recompute profile-level planner metrics and record-level classifier metrics on each resample. Do not replace them with unweighted averages of family/group scores.
step31_uncertainty_handoff.interpretation: Intervals describe sensitivity to the constructed benchmark cases, not real-athlete outcomes or training-seed variability.
step31_uncertainty_handoff.pairing: Keep matched model/version outcomes together within each sampled group and include every member of a drawn group with its multiplicity.
step31_uncertainty_handoff.status: planned; operational procedure and implementation pending Step 31

paired.version_mapping: V1 through V4 are fixed analyst aliases for the four planned workflows. Bind them to frozen runner/workflow versions before real evaluation; this cell assigns no actual run IDs.

planner.advisory_findings: Report advisory unknowns and violations separately; they do not alone fail the required-check primary measure. Essentiality follows the accepted request and adopted policy, not a blanket missing-history penalty.
planner.assessment_completeness: Checker errors and missing expected assessments remain external assessment failures. Retain known partial violations separately; do not convert an absent checker result into semantic unknown or a model violation.
planner.case_scoring_ready: An externally supplied prerequisite in artificial fixtures; not an implemented case-acceptance validator or proof of reference readiness.
planner.case_success: Require the designated returned response, valid shared parsing, required plan and activity content, request completeness, and every required applicable check met.

coverage.interpretation: Conclusive coverage is not a pass rate.
coverage.unit: expected parent checks, not number of activity instances

planner.empty_mask: A bare empty, missing or advisory-only obligation list cannot establish required-check readiness in this component. Reviewed non-applicability is an explicit required parent assessment with an evidence basis; required plan/completeness gates still apply. This readiness hold is not a planner failure.

evidence_ratios.attribution_coverage: Source-dependent claims with usable attribution / source-dependent claims reviewed
evidence_ratios.cited_claim_support: Supported cited claims / cited claims assessed
evidence_ratios.empty_denominator: Unavailable, with counts. No supplied IDs does not mean perfect attribution. ID validity and factual support remain separate.
evidence_ratios.id_validity: Resolvable distinct IDs / supplied distinct IDs

planner.execution: Unstarted or awaiting permitted resumption is incomplete. Terminal timeout, failed execution or missing designated response prevents success without requiring downstream activity assessments.
planner.expectation_boundary: Expected obligations and applicability must come from accepted private annotations and adopted public contracts/rules/policies before final outputs. This helper does not prepare or approve them.
planner.expected_instances: Instances needed for the parent condition, established by adopted applicability. Keep unrelated advisory/optional findings separate from required conditions.
planner.format_and_independence: Optional source-ID fields remain optional. Version4 internal acceptance does not determine the external outcome; earlier diagnostic drafts cannot replace the designated response after fatal execution.
planner.human_review: Preserve malformed but readable returned text for later independent human review; no automated human scores or reviewer decisions are assigned here.
planner.parent_aggregation: An established violation dominates. Otherwise necessary unknowns prevent met. Preserve all instance findings and evidence; justified non-applicability needs a reason and evidence reference.
planner.population_readiness: These counts are design targets. Do not calculate final rates from unaccepted drafts, drop failed jobs, or describe an incomplete experiment as complete.
planner.primary_measure: Successful feasible cases divided by all 150 accepted feasible final cases per version once the declared roster and assessment are complete.
planner.response_assessment: Malformed output, missing required plan, incomplete scope or omitted required activity content prevents success. Unavailable or failed external parsing/assessment remains incomplete.
planner.scope: Pure aggregation of supplied artificial facts. No planner text, profile content, rule thresholds, source lookups or model calls are evaluated.
planner.scoring_complete_scope: The case calculator's scoring_complete flag resolves its primary disposition only. A decisive missing response or incomplete-plan failure does not certify every ancillary assessment as finished. Preserve any existing checker-error ledger and unresolved coverage independently; this flag alone cannot finalize an experiment.

runtime.clock_cache_policy: Record timing method, device/software and warm/cold/cache behavior with each actual experiment; use a common setup policy across planner versions.
runtime.costs: The helper reports model-transport estimates only, with an amount, currency and recorded pricing/estimation basis per attempt. It does not establish billed charges, cost-free local compute, or full-workflow cost. Non-model retrieval/lookup/provider charges need a separate inventory. Never combine currencies; do not impute unknown costs as zero.
runtime.execution_only: Returned means the workflow returned, not that its plan passed independent scoring. Successful-response latency requires a later join to independent outcomes; preserve failed/timeout times separately.
runtime.model_usage_unit: One workflow job per call/attempt inventory. A transport attempt has one declared logical-call parent. Additional attempts on that parent count as retries; substantive revision calls have their own logical IDs.
runtime.resource_measurements: The later runner records available device/resource observations with metric, unit, device, measurement window and method. Missing GPU, RAM, energy, pricing or token telemetry remains unavailable. No resource probe or estimated utilization is run here.
runtime.resumption: The later runner must log run segments, active workflow timing, and any paused/offline interval separately under a frozen policy. Do not mix incompatible clock origins or reconstruct resumed wall time from a last-call duration.
runtime.roles_and_phases: Roles (generator/coordinator/specialist/evaluator) and phases (initial/revision) are separate overlapping breakdowns of the same logical calls. Do not add them together. Revision rounds count distinct declared model-call revision indices; non-model revision work needs its own stage observations.
runtime.stages: Stage durations can overlap or nest. Keep original IDs/observations; do not sum them into elapsed wall time. Common clock scope and instrumentation must be established by the runner.
runtime.startup: Record common startup/model-loading separately. If lazy loading happens inside a request timer it remains part of that request time and must not be subtracted. Startup observations are not added to the recorded request total.
runtime.summary_policy: Observed means/totals include available measurements only, with measured/missing counts. Complete totals/means stay null until the declared job inventory is terminal and all expected measurements are available. Pending/unrecorded jobs are unfinished work. Empty latency groups have no numerical latency.
runtime.summary_scopes: Retrieval/lookup count aggregates refer to terminal jobs only; pending-job count observations remain in their original records. Stage and startup observation counts describe all recorded jobs. Output scope labels identify this distinction; complete totals remain unavailable while jobs are pending.
runtime.tokens: Account input/output token usage once at transport-attempt level, including failures where usage is known. No logical-call token fields or sum of both levels. Missing usage remains null; observed partial totals carry availability counts.
runtime.usage_completion: Call and attempt inventories must be complete, attempts terminal, and each declared call represented by an attempt before complete usage totals are exposed. Failed/timeout attempts retain measured usage. Explicit zero counts/tokens are valid for a complete empty inventory.
runtime.workflow_timer: One observed whole-workflow request duration includes retrieval/lookup, orchestration, model calls, transport retries, revisions and in-request waiting. It is not reconstructed from the final call or a sum of stage durations.

privacy_boundary: Only public component manifests and aggregate preparation status; no private case identities, expectations, masks, feasibility witnesses, selected sample IDs or reviewer assignments.

reference_readiness.scope: Selected reference checkpoint only; recheck intended versions and runtime operations before acceptance.
